{{Top}} {{Otheruses|Bendu}} {{MultipleIssues|image|updatecontent=[[Thrawn: Alliances]]}} {{Character |type= |image=[[File:Bendu.png]] |name=Bendu |homeworld=[[Atollon]]''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' |birth= |death=[[2 BBY]], [[Atollon]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of the [[Battle of Atollon]] to [[2 BBY]]. Since "[[The Lothal Insurgency (2)]]" established that Bendu was [[Death|killed]] on [[Atollon]] during such events, he must have died in 2 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. |species=[[Force wielder]]{{EncyclopediaCite|The Lothal Insurgency (2)}} |gender=[[Gender|Male]]{{Databank|bendu|Bendu}} |pronouns=He/him''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]'' |height= |mass= |hair=[[Color|Auburn]] |feathers= |eyes=White |skin=Gray |cyber= |families= |parents= |partners= |siblings= |children= |affiliation=[[The Force]]{{Rebels|Zero Hour}} |masters= |apprentices=[[Kanan Jarrus]] {{C|Force-sight apprentice}} }} {{Quote|Jedi and Sith wield the Ashla and Bogan. The light and the dark. I'm the one in the middle. The Bendu.|Bendu|}} '''Bendu''' was a [[Gender|male]] [[Force wielder]] who resided on the remote [[planet]] of [[Atollon]] and claimed to represent the center of [[the Force]], between the [[Light side of the Force|light side]] and the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]]. Bendu encountered [[Jedi Knight]] [[Kanan Jarrus]] in [[2 BBY]]. He developed a friendly relationship with Kanan and his [[Padawan]] [[Ezra Bridger]] and helped the two [[Jedi]] repair their relationship and deal with their fears and anxieties. Despite his wisdom and powers, Bendu refused to take sides in any conflict, and was angered when Kanan called him a coward for not intervening during the [[Battle of Atollon]], which caused him to unleash a storm against both the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebel]] and [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] forces on Atollon. ==Biography== ===Early life=== An ancient [[Force wielder]], Bendu claimed to represent the center of [[the Force]], standing between the [[Light side of the Force|light]] and the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]]. As he rested peacefully on the [[planet]] [[Atollon]], Bendu acquired countless knowledge over the years of his lifespan as he meditated in the Force. During this time, he always chose not to interfere in the ways and teachings from the Jedi or Sith, but he chose to still aid force-sensitives, training them to overcome their fears and internal conflict through personal trials.''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' At some point in his life, Bendu became familiar with the Sith and the [[Holocron fusion|process]] of fusing Jedi and Sith holocrons together, witnessing the results and consequences of such a [[vergence]]. ===Mentoring Kanan=== [[File:Bendu_and_the_blind_man.png|thumb|left|250px|Bendu meeting Kanan]]{{Quote|An object cannot make you good or evil. The temptation of power, forbidden knowledge, even the desire to do good can lead some down that path. But only you can change yourself.|Bendu to Kanan|''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]''}} By [[2 BBY]],{{RebelsDate|301}} Bendu still lived on Atollon where the [[Phoenix Cell]] maintained a [[Chopper Base|base]]. At one point, Bendu called out to the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Kanan Jarrus]], who was [[Meditation|meditating]] outside Chopper Base. Kanan had retreated into meditation after losing his sight during a [[Mission to Malachor]]. Bendu called out to Kanan and eventually led him into a series of mesas in the wilderness. When Kanan finally arrived, Bendu told the [[Jedi]] Knight that his imbalance had awoken him from his slumber. After introducing himself, he allowed Kanan to identify himself as a Jedi Knight. Bendu listened as Kanan told him about his fear that his apprentice [[Ezra Bridger]] was falling to the dark side. When Kanan showed him the [[Sith holocron (Malachor)|Sith holocron]] that Ezra had obtained on [[Malachor]], Bendu explained that an object could not make someone good or evil. However, he stressed that only a person could choose to change themselves. Bendu then took an interest in Kanan's [[sensor beacon]], which the Jedi had used to ward off several [[krykna]], arachnid predators that were indigenous to Atollon. Bendu then destroyed the sensor marker. When Kanan protested, he told the Jedi that he would never regain his sight but that he could teach Kanan to see through his other senses. When Kanan agreed to take his lesson, Bendu instructed the Jedi to empty his mind, turn around and walk forward. Kanan was quickly surrounded by two krykna which did not attack him. Bendu then explained that Kanan's bad experience with creatures stemmed from not seeing them for what they actually were. Kanan began to make peace with the krykna but was startled when he sensed that Ezra was in danger. After igniting [[Kanan Jarrus' lightsaber|his]] [[lightsaber]], Kanan realized that the krykna had been feeding off his fear and emotions. When Kanan deduced that he had isolated himself from everyone and the Force, Bendu commented that he had finally regained his Force connection. Before leaving to [[Mission to Reklam Station|rescue]] Ezra, Kanan left the Sith holocron with Bendu. Bendu then inspected the object and laughed. ===Ezra's trials=== [[File:EzraAndKananMeetBendu-SWRS03E03.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ezra meets Bendu]] After the former [[Sith]] [[Maul]] kidnapped the other crew of the ''[[Ghost]]'', Kanan and Ezra traveled on a [[speeder bike]] to Bendu's lair in Atollon's wilderness. The two Jedi were surrounded by several krykna but Bendu awoke and scared them away. When Bendu asked the two Jedi whether they had come for a chat, Ezra related to the Force-wielder their predicament with Maul. Ezra and Kanan explained that Maul desired both the Sith holocron and [[Kanan Jarrus' holocron|Kanan's own]] Jedi holocron. While Bendu was unfamiliar with Maul, he remarked that the [[Holocron fusion|convergence]] of the Sith and Jedi holocrons would be dangerous.{{Rebels|The Holocrons of Fate}} Bendu corrected Ezra's view that the holocrons were merely libraries and pointed out that they could grant clarity of vision but also produce chaos. When Ezra reiterated that he needed the Sith holocron in order to save his friends, Bendu opined that the object was a source of imbalance between him and his master Kanan. However, he told him that he needed to enter a [[cave]] inhabited by krykna in order to retrieve the Sith holocron. Before entering the cave, Kanan instructed his apprentice to leave [[Sabine Wren's lightsaber|his lightsaber]] behind and to use a [[comlink]] instead. When asked why, Kanan explained that his apprentice needed to learn how to resolve problems without a lightsaber. Kanan then went in after him when Ezra's comlink was damaged by krykna, asking Bendu to keep an eye on their lightsabers. Remaining outside, Bendu remarked to himself and a curious [[dokma]] that perhaps the two would mend their bond or perhaps they would be eaten instead, but brushed off the latter option as being the way of things. The two Jedi successfully managed to retrieve the Sith holocron after a trial which involved Ezra learning to overcome his fear of the krykna and forgiving himself for the events on Malachor, mending the frayed bond between himself and his master; outside the cave, Bendu sensed this and smiled. After Ezra and Kanan returned from the cave, Bendu expressed satisfaction that the imbalance between master and apprentice had been resolved. However, he warned the two Jedi that their true test had just begun. Since Maul was unable to open the Jedi holocron, Bendu told the pair that the task would have to fall on one of them. When Ezra suggests they could wield the power of both holocrons, Bendu warned him that it came with a price. He stressed that once a secret was known, it could not be unknown. ===The spectre of Maul=== After Maul used the dark side of the Force to torment Ezra with [[Force vision]]s, Ezra and Kanan traveled into the wilderness to seek help from Bendu. Bendu had been expecting them and remarked that they were "not exactly quiet creatures." When Ezra told Bendu that Maul had resurfaced, Bendu replied that joining the holocrons together would bring great wisdom and danger at the same time. Ezra admitted that this was the price of his power and that his vision was incomplete because he let go before the holocrons could reveal their full secrets.{{Rebels|Visions and Voices}} Bendu remarked that this was not a good sign. When Bendu asked Ezra what he wanted, he advised Ezra and Kanan not to turn around. Despite his warnings, the two Jedi turned around and saw Maul watching them from atop a dune. When Kanan turned back around Bendu was gone. Maul then persuaded Ezra to come with him to [[Dathomir]] in return for keeping the location of Chopper Base a secret. Kanan and Sabine followed Maul and Ezra to Dathomir. Following a [[Skirmish on Dathomir|skirmish]] with the spirits of fallen [[Nightsisters]], they discovered that the [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] held the key to destroying the Sith. ===Sabine's test=== While the [[Mandalorian]] weapons expert [[Sabine Wren]] was undergoing instruction with the [[Darksaber]], she went to a rock to contemplate on her fears and struggles about her family. Ezra went to comfort her and reassured her that Kanan meant well. Realizing that Ezra was right, Sabine went into the wilderness to clear her mind. As she left, Bendu surfaced but did not initiate contact with her.{{Rebels|Trials of the Darksaber}} ===Battle of Atollon=== {{Quote|You cannot see. But I can.''"
"''What? What do you see?''"
"''I see your defeat. Like many arms surrounding you in a cold embrace.|Bendu and Grand Admiral Thrawn|}} [[File:Bendu_lighting_form.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Bendu as a storm throwing lightning.]] Eventually, [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] located the rebel forces at Atollon and [[Battle of Atollon|ambushed]] them there. Kanan went to the wilderness to seek out Bendu for help. However, Bendu refused to help Kanan in order to keep his neutrality and blamed him for bringing the war to Atollon. Kanan then called Bendu a coward, which led to Bendu rising into a ball of smoke and exclaiming that perhaps it was the will of the Force to destroy the Jedi "and all your kind," which he vowed to carry out. While Kanan returned to Chopper Base, the Empire initiated an [[orbital bombardment]] on Atollon. After Thrawn landed on Atollon and trapped the rebel leaders at Chopper Base, all were drawn to look at a gathering storm in the sky, with one bolt of lightning almost striking Thrawn himself. Two glowing yellow eyes appeared in the midst of the clouds and Bendu's echoing voice proclaimed his identity. He then cried "I bring [[death]]!" and unleashed powerful lightning strikes onto the ground, destroying two [[All Terrain Armored Transport|AT-AT walkers]] and several grounded rebel starfighters. Desiring his world to be left in peace, Bendu ordered both Rebels and Imperials alike to leave Atollon, killing several [[death trooper]]s with his lightning strikes as emphasis. Kanan and his fellow Rebels then attempted to flee on the ''Ghost;'' noticing the fleeing rebel ships, Bendu called out to Kanan by name and struck the ''Ghost'' with lightning, though not hard enough to destroy it. One A-wing was destroyed by him but the others escaped, so Bendu increased his onslaught on the Imperials, demanding again that they leave. Dismissing the attack as "Jedi devilry," Thrawn ordered his forces to shoot at the eye of the storm. Bendu was struck by fire coming from the remaining walkers and a squad of death troopers, causing the huge Force wielder to fall from the sky and crash to ground. [[File:Thrawn_Bendu_ZH.png|thumb|right|250px|Bendu warns Thrawn about his future.]] After the defeated rebel forces abandoned the system, Thrawn found Bendu lying wounded on the ground and asked him what sort of creature he was. The defiant Bendu replied that he was one far beyond Thrawn's power to destroy. When Thrawn disagreed, Bendu warned him that he could see where the [[Chiss]] could not; [[Liberation of Lothal|his defeat]], like "many arms surrounding him in a cold embrace." Angered and unnerved by this prediction, Thrawn attempted to finish Bendu by shooting him with his blaster, but the Force wielder vanished before the blast could touch him, becoming one with the Force while letting out a deep, echoing laugh of mockery that left the Chiss admiral highly unsettled. The Bendu's warning to Thrawn was eventually fulfilled when Ezra Bridger defeated the Grand Admiral aboard his flagship with the help of several [[purrgil]], the "many arms" of the creatures holding him in their "cold embrace," just as the Bendu had prophesied.{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}} ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|You have brought war to my quiet world, Kanan Jarrus, Jedi Knight. And I will have no part of it!|Bendu to Kanan Jarrus|}} [[File:Bendu_TVE.png|thumb|left|300px|Bendu was a massive and powerful being.]] Bendu was a wise and enigmatic being of an immense size. The Bendu resembled both a buffalo{{InsiderCite|216|Forces of Nature: The Wild Spaces and Wilder Creatures of the Star Wars Galaxy|Forces of Nature: The Wild Spaces and Wilder Creatures of the ''Star Wars'' Galaxy}} and giant rocky monolith with two eyes, a flat nose, and a long beard. He was a powerful entity who could control nature including the krykna spiders of Atollon. Bendu could also sense the presence of other Force-wielders from a distance. Despite his imposing appearance, Bendu presented himself as a gentle, wise and patient teacher who believed that other [[Force-sensitive]] beings needed to learn to overcome their fears and imbalances through personal trials. He taught Kanan how to overcome his blindness as well as his fear of krykna by teaching the Jedi Knight how to rely on his senses. While recognizing that the Sith holocron was dangerous, Bendu believed that only the user had the power to change themselves for better or worse. Bendu was immensely powerful and had the power to destroy a sensor marker with a mere flick of his hands. Bendu recognized that the convergence of Sith and Jedi holocrons had the power to produce clarity of vision but could also lead to chaos. He was concerned with the relationship between Kanan and his apprentice Ezra and believed that the two needed to repair it. Bendu was indifferent to the affairs and conflicts of the galaxy, wanting no part in the struggle and chaos that plagued it, enjoying balance and remaining firm in his neutral stance. He felt at peace living on Atollon and was angered when the rebels unintentionally lured the Empire to his planet. He was insulted when Kanan pleaded for him to break his neutrality and fight the Empire. Bendu was ambivalent to the galaxy's problems. Despite his patience, wisdom, and powers, Bendu entered into a rage when Kanan accused him of cowardice for not wanting to help the rebels during the Battle of Atollon, showing a degree of pride and a desire for respect. Still, Bendu was not intimidated by Thrawn even after being wounded by him and predicted the Grand Admiral's defeat. ==Powers and abilities== {{Quote|I bring death!|Bendu unleashing his power|}} Bendu was Force-sensitive, his connection being great, as was his power in the Force. Bendu was an immensely powerful being who possessed incredible connections to the Force and could perceive the emotions of others. He also had the power to [[Teleportation (Force power)|appear and disappear at will]]. Despite his ability to create powerful storms by manipulating the nature around him, he was knocked to the ground when Grand Admiral Thrawn directed artillery fire at him. Bendu also had the [[Precognition|power of foresight]] and predicted Thrawn's defeat. After warning Thrawn about his future, Bendu laughed and disappeared as Thrawn shot at him. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|You are set on this confrontation then?''"
"''I have to know the truth.''"
"''So be it, but understand this, much will change as a result of this encounter, including you.''"
"''Isn't that true of all things, as time advances?''"
"''My dear, when I say change, I mean death.''"
"''So I will die?''"
"''Will you? I didn't know that. Goodbye then, Ahsoka Tano, former Jedi Knight.|Bendu and Ahsoka Tano, prior to Tano's confrontation with her former master|{{Twitter|dave_filoni|status/883124880157192192|[[Dave Filoni]]|date=2017-07-27|archivefile=File:AhsokaBenduMeeting.jpg}}}} [[File:AhsokaandBendu.png|thumb|right|200px|Bendu meets with Ahsoka Tano]] Bendu was created and developed for the [[Star Wars Rebels Season Three|third season]] of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'', and made his debut in the season's first episode, ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]''. The character is voiced by famed [[Wikipedia:Doctor Who|''Doctor Who'']] actor [[Tom Baker]].{{SW|url=news/swce-2016-11-things-we-learned-from-the-star-wars-rebels-season-three-panel|text=SWCE 2016: 11 Things We Learned From the ''Star Wars Rebels'' Season Three Panel|date=2016-07-16|nolive=1}} Due to studio secrecy, no one except executive producer [[Dave Filoni]] told Baker anything about the character he was voicing. When voicing Bendu, who was described as a "life force", the actor drew on his own religious upbringing ("believing in angels, devils, divine forces and other worlds") and embraced in his imagination all the thoughts he had from his past.{{WebCite|url=http://usatoday.com/story/life/tv/2016/09/15/tom-baker-star-wars-rebels-exclusive-clip/90410988|text='Doctor Who' star Tom Baker is a Force in 'Star Wars Rebels'|author=Brian Truitt|date=2016-09-15|work=''[[Wikipedia:USA Today|USA Today]]''|archivedate=20220129014858}} The term "Bendu" first appeared in the [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of the script for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']] as the name of the Jedi Knights, the "[[Jedi-Bendu]]."[[The Star Wars rough draft|''The Star Wars'' rough draft]] In the ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' episode [[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow|Steps Into Shadow]], Bendu refers to the [[Light side of the Force|Light side]] and [[Dark side of the Force|Dark side]] of [[the Force]] as "the Ashla and the Bogan."''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]'' In the [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|second draft]] of the script for ''A New Hope'', the Light side is called "the Ashla" and the Dark side is called "the Bogan."''[[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars]]'' After the conclusion of the third season, series executive producer Dave Filoni revealed that [[Ahsoka Tano]] met Bendu during the events of "[[The Mystery of Chopper Base]]." Though these events were never depicted on screen, Filoni tweeted dialogue from their encounter as well as artwork illustrating the event. During their conversation, Bendu mentioned Tano's upcoming confrontation with her [[Anakin Skywalker|former master]]. When Tano explained that she had to know the truth, Bendu retorted that everything would change as a result of their encounter, including her. As the [[Togruta]] failed to see his point, he clarified that "change" meant death. Tano asked then if she would die, but Bendu acted as if she was affirming it, and so replied that he did not know that before telling her goodbye. ==Appearances== *''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]'' {{1st}} *{{Rebels|The Holocrons of Fate}} *{{Rebels|Visions and Voices}} *{{Rebels|Trials of the Darksaber}} *{{Rebels|Zero Hour}} *''[[Thrawn: Alliances]]'' {{Ab|Thrawn: Alliances (audiobook)}} {{Imo}} ==Sources== {{ScrollBox|content= *{{SWYouTube|xmXp802sFgQ|Star Wars Rebels Season Three Trailer (Official)|sw_url=video/star-wars-rebels-season-three-trailer}} *{{SW|url=news/swce-2016-11-things-we-learned-from-the-star-wars-rebels-season-three-panel|text=SWCE 2016: 11 Things We Learned From the ''Star Wars Rebels'' Season Three Panel|nolive=1}} *{{SWYouTube|mup7aH5LK_Y|Meet Bendu -
